title: Autonomic Disorders Fellowship
inst: University of Utah School of Medicine (University of Utah Health)
Duration: 1 year, with an optional second year (clinical, research or combined tracks)
Deadline: Applications open 1 March of PGY-3 year; deadline 1 October of PGY-4 (final residency) year; offers made on a rolling basis 31 October-31 December
Eligibility: Graduate of an ACGME-, RCPSC- or CanERA-accredited residency in adult neurology, child neurology, cardiology or internal medicine; must be a US citizen or permanent resident
International applicants: Not open to non-US citizens/non-permanent residents: page states applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents (ECFMG certificate requested if applicable)
Accreditation: UCNS-accredited Autonomic Disorders fellowship (listed in the UCNS Fellowship Directory)
Application method: Contact the programme (neuro.fellowship@hsc.utah.edu) to apply; CV, personal statement, three letters of recommendation, USMLE/COMLEX scores and ECFMG certificate if applicable
Visa support: No visa route: US citizenship or permanent residency required
Summary: UCNS-accredited one- or two-year fellowship at the University of Utah training fellows in autonomic testing, autonomic neurology and complex dysautonomia care, with clinical, research or combined tracks.

title: Autonomic Disorders Fellowship (Autonomic Neurology and Neurogastroenterology tracks)

Accreditation: UCNS-accredited Autonomic Disorders fellowship (listed in the UCNS Fellowship Directory)

Positions: 2 clinical fellows per year (one autonomic neurology, one neurogastroenterology)
Licence requirement: Current valid and unrestricted medical licence to practise in California required
Summary: UCNS-accredited one-year clinical fellowship in autonomic neurology and neurogastroenterology covering autonomic function testing, skin biopsy and clinical research at Stanford.

title: Movement Disorders Fellowship
inst: University of Minnesota Medical School
Deadline: Register with SF Match 1 April-15 May; completed application downloadable through SF Match by 1 July; ranking in early September
Eligibility: Completing an ACGME-accredited neurology residency and ABPN board eligible before start; eligible for a full Minnesota Board licence
International applicants: Does not accept J-1 visa holders (does not participate in the ACGME NST Program)
Accreditation: Not stated on official page
Application method: SF Match Central Application Service
Visa support: No J-1: the fellowship does not participate in the ACGME NST Program and does not accept J-1 visa holders
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a full Minnesota Board licence
Summary: Two-year University of Minnesota fellowship with intensive clinical movement disorders training in year one and an independent patient panel, DBS surgical practice and Udall Center research in year two.

title: Multiple Sclerosis Fellowship
